result.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
result.summary: In this work, we study whether frontier agent can continually improve real-world AI infrastructure over long horizons. We introduce Infrathon, a benchmark of diverse, long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization tasks across different levels. We evaluate six models across 150 runs with 24-hour budgets, totaling over 10,000 GPU-hours. Our results show that model rankings vary with the evaluation horizon, while 135 of the 150 runs achieve further improvements during the second half of their budgets. These findings indicate that shorter evaluations can overlook both optimization gains and changes in relative model performance. We also find agents can discover solutions that outperform human-designed baselines: Claude Opus 5.5 increases the mean KV-cache compression ratio from 6.82% with the human-designed Quant-VideoGen codec to 19.86%. Analysis of agent trajectories identifies task violations, unreliable testing, and premature completion as barriers to sustained improvement. Together, Our Infrathon framework provide resources for constructing long-horizon tasks, evaluating frontier agents, and discovering good infrastructure solutions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Infrathon 基准，用 24 小时预算的长期程任务评估语言 agent 持续优化 AI 基础设施的能力，并分析优化轨迹中的失败模式（任务违规、测试不可靠、过早结束）。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其长期程评估显示模型排序随预算长度变化、多数运行在后半段才继续改进，可供核查 LVR 中 STOP 决策、计算预算分配与长度泛化评价的设定是否受评估时程影响。
